findings.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts inside multiword proper names or titles, treating internal boundaries as acceptable splits and so fragmenting named entities.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1527','en_us_152','en_us_1179','en_us_288','en_us_381','en_us_1296'] then what they share — each source contains a multiword proper name or title (two or more adjacent capitalized words) that the policy split but the target kept intact
findings.type_predicate: a multiword proper name: two or more adjacent words that each start with a capital letter (e.g. personal name, organization, treaty or official title)

edit.text: Do not cut inside multiword proper names or titles (two or more adjacent capitalized words); keep such name sequences intact.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt cuts immediately after fronted temporal/adverbial phrases, detaching them from their governing verb and producing incoherent or misleading early pieces.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1179','en_us_152','en_us_381','en_us_1615','en_us_1412'] then what they share — each source begins with a fronted temporal or adverbial phrase (e.g. 'In 1895,', 'Then, a few years later', 'At the extremes of the poll,') that the policy separated from its main clause
findings.type_predicate: an initial/fronted temporal or adverbial phrase that ends with a comma (e.g. starts the sentence and is followed by a comma)

edit.text: Keep fronted adverbials/temporal adjuncts attached to their main clause: do not cut immediately after an initial adverbial phrase ending in a comma.

findings.diagnosis: When forced to choose between two imperfect internal cuts, the prompt prefers cuts that break verb–object adjacency; instead it should prefer cuts that avoid separating a verb from its core object/complement.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_633','en_us_1113','en_us_381','en_us_1116'] then what they share — each sentence offers two internal cut candidates where one would split a verb from its object/complement while the other splits earlier material; the measurement prefers keeping verb and object together
findings.type_predicate: a clause containing two candidate cut positions: one cut lies between a finite verb and its core direct object or essential complement, the other cut lies earlier in the clause (e.g. between subject or initial adjunct and that verb)

edit.text: When ordering two internal cuts in the same clause, prefer the cut that does not separate a verb from its direct object or essential complement; keep verbs adjacent to their core arguments.
